item: A read that fails on a damaged page of an encrypted file no longer leaves its pooled connection poisoned
summary: On an encrypted library (SQLCipher) the first read of a page that fails its check left that connection answering an empty MemoryError to every later page read, healthy tables included, until it was closed (measured; rollback, commit, shrink_memory and a second key do not clear it, and a plain SQLite connection is not affected). A pooled connection went back in that state, so one request that touched a damaged page left a connection that failed every later request with the text of a real out-of-memory until the process restarted. The damage observer (damage.discard_poisoned_connection, called from the handle_error listener attach registers) now marks a SQLCipher SQLITE_CORRUPT (primary code 11) as a disconnect for that one connection and keeps the rest of the pool (invalidate_pool_on_disconnect off); the pool opens a fresh connection on the next checkout and the error the caller sees is still the corruption error. A MemoryError, a wrong key (code 26) and a plain SQLite file's corruption are never reclassified. tests/test_poisoned_connection.py runs on real encrypted stores, including the canary that the poison is still there without the observer.
